payload.feature:
FIX ROUND 717g3 for story #717, decision 0091 slice 3d's FIRST FIX (gaps 3, 4 and 5 of what `brokkr init` scaffolds), on branch story-717-init-gaps. It is checked out in this worktree at 8ca33661, which is 4e9c4fb3 (the story, rebased onto main 9be5d53d) plus fix round 717g2's commit. When you are done, the branch is 8ca33661 plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main.

WHERE IT STANDS:
- 4e9c4fb3, the story. Its review stopped at REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD: an install root could be a directory holding credentials.
- 8ca33661, fix round 717g2 (fix-round-717g2-for-story-717-de-70e0ebd3). It added the four `Layout`s, `holds_only`, and the execute check. Its review stopped at REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD AGAIN, and the chief reproduced both findings below on a binary built at HEAD.
- The chief CONFIRMED and keeps:
  - reproduction (b) (`~/.aws/bin` beside credentials) refused, naming 'credentials';
  - reproduction (a) not binding `~/.local/share`;
  - `too_broad` as the backstop;
  - `HOST_TOOLCHAIN_BINDS` adding no bind for `/usr/local`-like roots;
  - the four layouts naming no dotfile and no credential;
  - gap 4 (the base grant), gap 5 (`--locked`), the docs, and the compose-level tests.
- The chief's gates: `init::` 30 passed, and the three init_stacks tests passed. The panel reports fmt, clippy, the nine-suite integration gate (189 passed, 1 ignored), witness_digests:: (6), typos, the ratchets and git diff --check all clean.

THE RULINGS THAT BIND IT:
- 2026-10-20, "accept all for 0090" (PR #793, renumbered 0091): decision 0091 is accepted. Its ruling 2: the folder's verifier is what `init` writes.
- 2026-10-22, in chat, verbatim: "accept all as recommended" (#717, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/717#issuecomment-6351117518). For gap 3 that means:
  - `init` resolves `npm` and `node` to their install and binds it read-only on verify's box;
  - with no npm found, `init` says so, and verify fails closed with that text;
  - never bind `$HOME` itself, `~/.local` whole, or any directory holding credentials.
- 2026-10-23, in chat, verbatim: "keep the hold, go with node.rs" (#717, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/717#issuecomment-6360189312). adapters.rs's hold stays, and node.rs asks the kernel the exec question itself (finding 2).
- Decision 0071 rulings 3, 5, 8 and 9. 2026-09-26, the threat model: catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. Linux and macOS only (decision 0063).

THE INVARIANT (unchanged from 717g2), inside and outside `$HOME`: nothing `init` binds holds an entry that is not part of the runner's install. Where `init` can't tell, it refuses with `Reach::Unbindable`, and verify fails closed with init's sentence.

THE BAR, set by the controller so this round can close:
- A **tool-managed home** (volta's root, bun's root, pnpm's home) is the install. It is bound whole once its top-level entries pass `holds_only`. What lies under its named entries is the tool's own, so planting files deep inside one is not the realistic misuse this threat model asks you to catch.
- A **node prefix** is NOT tool-managed. It can't be told apart from a shared prefix (`/opt`, `~/opt`, `~/sw`) whose `share`, `include` or `bin` also hold other software. So a node prefix is never bound whole: see finding 1 (ii).

THE FINDINGS TO FIX:
1. **HIGH, security** (raised by adversarial; the chief reproduced it on a binary built at HEAD).
   - **What's wrong:**
     - node.rs `root()` (:304-320) still roots a plain-file runner at its PATH directory's PARENT whenever that directory is named `bin`. It classifies that parent as `Layout::NodePrefix` from the basename alone.
     - `holds_only()` (:325-338) checks only the TOP-LEVEL names, so anything under `share`, `include`, `lib` or `bin` is bound whole.
     - `mount_binds` (brokkr-protocol hands/sealed.rs:206-230) ro-binds the whole source.
   - **The chief's reproduction:** a temp dir holds executable (0755) plain files `opt/bin/{npm,node}` and `opt/share/keyrings/user.keystore`, beside a fresh repo with a package.json. Run `HOME=<tmp>/home PATH=<tmp>/opt/bin:/usr/bin:/bin brokkr init .`. It exits 0 with binds `[{"mode":"ro","path":"<tmp>/opt"}]`, and the keystore is inside the bind.
   - The test `a_plain_runner_outside_home_binds_no_directory_holding_others` plants `opt/etc`, a name NodePrefix already rejects, so it can't see this.
   - **THE SHAPE TO BUILD** (the chief's recommendation, extended to close the link variant too, which the same panel would try next):
     - (i) **A runner whose real file stands directly in its PATH directory** (`install.real.parent() == Some(&install.dir)`) is NEVER walked to a parent. `init` binds THAT FILE, read-only, as its own bind.
       - The one exception is a volta shim (real file `volta-shim`). It execs the images under its root's `tools`, so it keeps the volta root, `Layout::Volta`, and `holds_only`, as now.
       - This covers the chief's reproduction, bun's `~/.bun/bin/bun`, a standalone pnpm at `$PNPM_HOME/pnpm`, and a `node` binary in any `bin`.
       - **Confirm that a file bind works**, and cite each line you read:
         - `hands.rs` `Bind` (path, mode, mask) puts no directory constraint on the path.
         - `sealed.rs` `source()` (:190-195) canonicalises the path and records its dev/ino.
         - `mount_binds` uses `Mount::RoBindTry`, which bwrap applies to a file.
         - A mask on a file source is a no-op: `from.join(name).exists()` is false.
         - Say whether the hands schema in contracts/ allows a file path (READ it, don't change it).
         - If you can run a real box here, show a bound file being executed. If you can't, say so; the controller's host check runs it.
     - (ii) **A runner whose real file resolves OUTSIDE its PATH directory** (a link into `../lib/node_modules/…`) walks to its layout root as now, and the root's top-level entries pass `holds_only` as now. That keeps reproduction (b)'s link form refused, naming 'credentials'. Then:
       - **Volta, Bun, PnpmHome:** bind the root whole, as now.
       - **NodePrefix:** bind `<prefix>/bin` and `<prefix>/lib/node_modules`, never the prefix itself. `include`, `share` and the release files are not needed to run node or npm. `lib/node_modules` is npm's own global package directory, so it is the install.
       - `<prefix>/bin` must hold only:
         - a regular file named `node`;
         - links whose canonical target lies under `<prefix>/lib/node_modules` (npm, npx, corepack, and global packages' bins).

         Any other entry refuses as `Unbound::Foreign(Layout::NodePrefix, <entry>)`, with the refusal naming it. Here `<entry>` is spelled as `bin/<name>`, or say how you spell it.
       - If `<prefix>/lib/node_modules` is missing or not a directory, refuse with `Unreadable` (or a variant you name).
     - (iii) **A bind under another bind is dropped**, so that an nvm `bin/node` file bind under its `bin` directory bind is not written twice. Binds keep their found order otherwise.
     - (iv) **`Reach::Found.binds` and the `bundle.json` shape:** say whether a file bind is spelled like a directory bind (`~/`-relative under HOME). If the type changes, keep it private to init.
   - **Update the module doc** (node.rs:1-27) and the docs card (docs/guides/cards/node.md) to say what is bound now: one sentence each, no more.

2. **MEDIUM, correctness** (correctness C1 and glm raised it; adversarial confirmed it; the chief reproduced it).
   - **What's wrong:** node.rs `install()` (:253) admits a candidate on `mode & 0o111 != 0`, which asks whether ANYONE may execute it. The ruled fix skips what THIS user can't run, as PATH lookup does.
   - **Reproduction:** `~/bin/npm`, owned by the user at mode 0641, stands ahead of an executable `opt/node/bin/{npm,node}`. `command -v npm` prints the later one, but init printed the "installed under <home>" refusal with no binds.
   - The house's answer is brokkr-protocol adapters/composite.rs:2191-2215, `effective_exec_access`: `rustix::fs::accessat(CWD, path, Access::EXEC_OK, AtFlags::EACCESS)`. Its doc records this exact 0641 case.
   - **THE OPERATOR RULED THIS, 2026-10-23, in chat, verbatim:** "keep the hold, go with node.rs" (#717, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/717#issuecomment-6360189312). The chief had recommended making that fn public and calling it. That needs `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs`'s `pub use composite::{…}` (:37), and adapters.rs stays under the operator's HOLD. So DON'T touch brokkr-protocol. Instead:
     - In node.rs, ask the kernel the same question: `rustix::fs::accessat(rustix::fs::CWD, &real, Access::EXEC_OK, AtFlags::EACCESS).is_ok()`, alongside `is_file()`. brokkr-cli already depends on rustix with "fs" (Cargo.toml:79).
     - A doc comment names composite.rs's `effective_exec_access` as the same kernel question, and says why it isn't shared yet.
   - **Name the consolidation in your notes as an INFO follow-up** for when the hold lifts: one home for "runnable", called by composite.rs, node.rs and hands/namespace.rs:438, which still carries the older `mode & 0o111` form (0071 ruling 5). Don't touch namespace.rs: decision 0065 slice two works in brokkr-protocol.

TESTS: exact values, each with a removal control recorded in the commit message. Do removal controls in a scratch copy, never with `git stash`, which is shared across worktrees.
- **The chief's reproduction**, in node/tests.rs:
  - Plant `opt/bin/{npm,node}` as 0755 plain files and `opt/share/keyrings/user.keystore`. The result is `Reach::Found` whose binds are exactly the two files, with no `opt` and no `opt/bin` directory.
  - Removal control: restore the bin-parent root for plain files. The test fails with the `opt` bind it wrote.
- **The link variant:**
  - Plant `opt/bin/npm → ../lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js` (a 0755 file), `opt/bin/node` (0755) and `opt/share/keyrings/user.keystore`. The binds are exactly `opt/bin` and `opt/lib/node_modules`, with no `opt` and no `share`.
  - Removal control: bind the NodePrefix root whole. The test fails naming `opt`.
- **A foreign entry in a node prefix's `bin`:** the link variant plus `opt/bin/credentials`, a plain file, is `Unbindable` with the exact sentence, and the binds are empty.
  - Removal control: drop the bin-entry check.
- **Reproduction (b), both forms:**
  - Its LINK form (`~/.aws/bin/npm` linking into `~/.aws/lib/node_modules/npm/…`, beside `~/.aws/credentials`) is refused naming 'credentials', as now.
  - Its PLAIN-FILE form binds exactly the two files and never `~/.aws`. Say so in a comment: no directory holding credentials is bound.
  - The compose-level `an_npm_beside_credentials_binds_nothing_and_fails_verify_closed` (tests/init_stacks.rs:1016) moves to the LINK form, so it still fails verify closed with the same sentence.
- **Re-pin the moved expectations from the tests' own reported values:**
  - the standalone pnpm now binds its file;
  - the nvm version directory now binds `bin` and `lib/node_modules`;
  - `each_layout_binds_whole_until_it_holds_one_entry_more` keeps Volta, Bun and PnpmHome whole, and checks NodePrefix's new binds;
  - the volta shim still binds the volta root.
- **The execute check:**
  - **Shadow:** an `npm` owned by the test user at 0641, earlier on PATH than a 0755 one, resolves to the 0755 one.
  - **Only one:** a 0641 `npm` alone gives `Reach::Missing("npm")`.
  - Mirror composite/tests.rs:2237's `privileged` guard: as root, 0641 is executable to the kernel, so the assertions switch.
  - Removal control: restore `mode & 0o111`. The shadow test fails with the 0641 install's Reach.
- The compose-level volta test (init_stacks::a_volta_npm_folder_binds_the_volta_root_on_verify) still passes. Every init digest that moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values.

GATES (all clean, from the worktree root):
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked init:: (timeout 590)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- init_stacks:: init_doctor:: brokkr_folder:: folder_seats:: doc_samples:: doc_truth:: suppressions:: portable_recipes:: recipes:: shelf:: (timeout 590)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it --locked -- witness_digests:: (no recipe witness should move)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- No contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ change. Nothing in brokkr-protocol. Don't touch doctor* (decision 0065 slice two), init.rs's codex arm (about :860) or init/claims.rs (the codex story, 717x), or anything dsh-specific (717d).
- SIZE: keep this round to init/node.rs, its tests, the one compose-level test and the two doc sentences. The story plus 717g2 already came to about +1,270 lines. If the shape needs much more, stop and say why.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's: capability_broker tests under host load (#743); the handoff status-pipe stage poll (#811's second half); the masking test's unasked case on macOS (#843). If one fails alone, rerun it on the host alone (`-- --exact`), quote both results, and carry on.

RULES
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), with the message "init: … (#717)" in the repository's style. Name both findings, the file-bind rule, the node prefix's two binds, the exec check as the operator ruled it ("keep the hold, go with node.rs"), and each removal control. End it with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- The implement phase alone changes files and commits. Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree: its .git file points at this worktree's gitdir, so git commands there move this HEAD.
- Run every command in the foreground. Never end your turn with a background job pending.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed.

The review judges:
- The invariant holds for every bind `init` can write, inside and outside HOME, at the bar above. Both of the chief's reproductions and the link variant are closed.
- A file bind reaches the box, with each line cited.
- The tool-managed homes still bind, and PATH lookup asks the kernel.
- Nothing else in 8ca33661 moved.

The review does NOT re-litigate the bar, or the operator's ruling on the exec check. It names any NEW ask for the operator.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-b9 or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- #717's codex story (717x: init.rs :860, init/claims.rs) and dsh doctor story (717d: doctor*) are queued after this.
- #753's seat_summary story is in brokkr-store, brokkr-core and brokkr-cli doctor/paths.
- Decision 0065 slice two (another session) is in brokkr-protocol and brokkr-runtime.
- crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs is under an operator HOLD.
- None is in init/node.rs.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

native.reason: dsh declares mcp and tool_permissions unsupported, which establishes only that Brokkr cannot narrow or extend its tool surface from the command line; it does not establish that dsh has no native egress of its own. On the contrary, recipes/research-dsh/README.md records that since dsh 0.1.2-rc.1 the headless profile ships web-fetch-http with page fetch on and a keyed search, so native egress is likely present and no OFF control for it has been declared or measured. Its native inventory, and any ON or OFF control for it, remain unmeasured: nothing is granted through dsh and no native denial is claimed (decision 0065 slice one; owed to the controller)

exec runs whatever command the bundle names; the engine cannot certify what an arbitrary child program reaches on its own, so its native inventory is unmeasured. Its hands, boundary and command authority are decisions 0043 and 0046's, unchanged

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff

One signed-off commit, 2e135854 on 8ca33661 (+347/-148, four files). Nothing in contracts/, fixtures/, policy/, reference/ or brokkr-protocol: `git diff 8ca33661 --stat` on those paths was empty.

FINDING 1 (HIGH).
(i) A runner whose real file stands directly in its PATH directory is never walked to a parent. init binds the one file, as the entry PATH reaches (dir/<name>), read-only. For a plain file that entry is the real file. For a same-directory link such as bunx -> bun, the entry is the link, and its sealed source canonicalises to the real file. I bound the entry rather than the real file so the name PATH looks up exists in the box. A volta shim is the one exception: it keeps its root, Layout::Volta and holds_only.
(ii) A runner whose real file resolves outside its PATH directory walks to its root, and the root's top-level entries pass holds_only, as before. Volta, Bun and PnpmHome are bound whole. A NodePrefix binds `bin` (the PATH directory) and `lib/node_modules`, never the prefix itself:
- `lib/node_modules` must canonicalise to its own path and be a directory; otherwise the refusal is Unbound::Unreadable.
- `bin` may hold only a regular file named `node` and entries whose canonical target lies under lib/node_modules. Anything else refuses as Foreign(NodePrefix, "bin/<name>"). A `bin` that can't be listed is Unreadable.
(iii) A bind under another bind is dropped (Found::spelled); found order is otherwise kept.
(iv) A file bind is spelled like a directory bind (~/-relative under HOME, {path, mode: ro}), and Reach's type is unchanged; a test asserts this shape and the verifier's PATH line.

FILE BIND REACHES THE BOX, from code I read:
- hands.rs:137-141: Bind {path, mode, mask} puts no constraint on what the path is.
- sealed.rs:190-195: source() canonicalises the path and records its dev/ino.
- sealed.rs:220: an ro bind mounts with Mount::RoBindTry, the same mount namespace.rs:186 uses for the resolv.conf file.
- sealed.rs:225: a mask on a file source is a no-op, because from.join(name).exists() is false.

- contracts/run-manifest.v13.schema.json:117: the bind path is {type: string, minLength: 1}. I read it and did not change it.
